title: Smooth, then differentiate
experiment: Removing the Gaussian smoothing stage lets the derivative filter turn pixel noise into false edges, which is the argument of §2–§3.
archetype_reason: Edge detection is a fixed chain (image → smooth → gradient → threshold) whose intermediates carry the argument.

fixed.image: 48×48, a square and a disk at intensity 1 on 0
fixed.edge_scale: a clean unit step gives Sobel magnitude 4

source.quote: a derivative filter applied to a noisy image responds to every pixel-level fluctuation
Smoothing with a Gaussian of width σ before differentiating suppresses those responses
An edge is declared wherever the gradient magnitude exceeds a threshold.

metrics.name: false_rate
metrics.label: false edges
metrics.meaning: fraction of pixels more than 2 px from any true edge that are marked as edges

metrics.name: recall
metrics.label: edges found
metrics.meaning: fraction of true edge pixels with a detection within 1 px

reproduce.claim: With σ = 1.5 at noise 0.25, almost no flat pixel is marked as an edge and most true edges are found.

source.quote: suppresses those responses, while true edges, which extend over many pixels, survive.

contrast.claim: Without smoothing the same threshold marks at least 10% more of the flat pixels as edges.

source.quote: thresholding its output marks edges all over flat regions.
